title: Long-tail request profiling, adaptive admission, and tenant fairness pilot
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: After the Feb capacity event we observed long-tail requests from a small set of tenants that inflated queue residency and blocked prefetch/autoscale signals. This ticket pilots a telemetry-driven approach to: (1) classify long-tail and bursty request patterns, (2) apply a differential soft-admission policy (short-grace window + probabilistic evict) for offenders, and (3) surface tenant-level fairness metrics in Console for SRE and product review. Goal: reduce queue buildup and improve autoscaler responsiveness without hard-cutting latency for polite tenants.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Ava Martinez: Added initial incident excerpts and heatmap of per-tenant queue residency (Confluence). Observed top 10 tenants contributed 48% of requests that spent >2x median queue time.

2026-03-04 — Ravi Shah: Spike profiling implemented in staging: sample 1% of requests and capture arrival, enqueue, dequeue, GPU-start, GPU-end timestamps. Early results show tail skew correlates with >512-token sequences + complex sampling-based generation.
2026-03-07 — Mei Chen (SRE): Raised concern that aggressive eviction may violate SLA for reserved Dedicated customers; suggested tenant-tier-aware rules and an opt-out for Dedicated pools.
2026-03-09 — Product: Request to add a console metric for "tenant-queue-residency-percentile" and an alert when a single tenant accounts for >20% of 99th percentile queue time over 10m.
2026-03-11 — Design review (Liam O'Connor): Suggested UI copy and visualization for fairness scores; recommended showing historical trend and last-mitigated action for transparency.
2026-03-13 — Ravi Shah: Implemented soft-admission circuit in staging with following knobs: grace_window_ms, max_probabilistic_evict_pct, tenant_tier_exemptions. Running 24h soak.
2026-03-14 — SRE: Early soak shows 22% reduction in 95th queue residency for non-exempt tenants and autoscaler ROS-keystroke triggered faster scale-up in two simulated bursts.
2026-03-14 — PM (Eleanor Wu): Good first step. Need follow-up to measure false positive rate for evictions and customer complaints over next 2 weeks.
action_items: Add lightweight per-request tracing fields to hosted API (arrival_ts, enqueue_ts, dequeue_ts, gpu_start_ts, gpu_end_ts) — ENG-624802
Build tenant profiling job (hourly) to compute 50/90/95/99 queue residency percentiles and a "fairness_score" — ENG-624803
Implement soft-admission controller with tenant-tier exemptions and per-tenant probabilistic eviction — PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/6872
Expose fairness metrics and recent mitigation actions in Console; wire alert for 10m windows where single tenant >20% of 99th residencies — design ticket DES-210

Create playbook entries for SRE runbook: how to interpret fairness scores, how to adjust knobs and opt a tenant out for Dedicated pools — runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/GC-queue-fairness
Run 2-week staged experiment: 50% traffic -> staged controller with conservative knobs; 25% -> aggressive; monitor customer complaints and error budgets
Post-experiment review and decision: adopt globally / adopt per-region / abandon and pursue alternative (e.g., prewarming + tenant quotas)
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry shows >=15% reduction in 95th queue residency for non-exempt hosted tenants during test bursts compared to baseline
No Dedicated tenant experiences >5% increase in end-to-end P99 latency attributable to soft-admission in pilot
Console surfaces tenant fairness metric and a per-tenant mitigation action timeline
SRE runbook updated and validated by on-call during an injected burst test
Experiment plan and results documented in Confluence and reviewed in postmortem follow-up meeting
